Now routed through the proven **`gate_rmw`** (read+mutate+write under one per-path lock, off-thread), so a save lands before or after but never inside. The per-path Mutex the editor's `write_note` also takes is held across the WHOLE read→modify→write; runs on the existing `thread::spawn` worker (no dispatch freeze; gate_rmw's two hard rules honoured — pure closure, DB-mirror update after). Behaviour-preserving + an idempotent-skip. cargo check + 31 sources + 22 write_gate tests pass; the primitive's serialization is proven by `concurrent_writers_serialize_never_tear`. **Reproduce-First** = the race window is visible in the old code (unlocked read → concurrent write → gate_write clobber) + the fix inherits gate_rmw's proof.
> - **The sweep (`wf_4dd12a39-694`, 46 agents, 24 confirmed):** the PJ-071 diff's own gate_rmw change = **ZERO findings**. **Version 3.40 | 2026-07-12**

> **What changed in v3.40** (**PJ-070 — the watcher external-change APP-KILLER — SHIPPED + Boss-validated end-to-end + `/migration` CLOSED. An external `.md` edit (git-pull / Syncthing / Obsidian) to an OPEN note is no longer silently clobbered by the next keystroke — it is adopted into the single-ownership note model (clean → adopt + remount; unsaved-conflict → a `.conflict` side-copy + banner, zero loss). The first Group-1 safety item off the re-prioritized backlog.** Ultracode):
> - **The bug (the main-window mirror of the closed G3 cross-window class).** Under Single-Ownership (MIG-076) the open editor's source of truth is the in-memory note **model**, not the store's `tab.content`. The watcher flush (`+layout.svelte`) updated only `tab.content` — it never adopted the disk into the model or bumped `reloadVersion` — so the mounted editor kept the **stale** body and the debounced `editor_save` durably overwrote the external edit, then reindexed so search agreed with the stomp. Reproduced deterministically (`tests/mig-076` **Recipe O**) + confirmed on the running app.
> - **The fix (Boss-ratified Option B + the `.conflict`-sidecar conflict policy).** One shared, harness-testable store helper **`adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs(paths, hooks, readDisk)`** that BOTH main-window ingress paths call (the watcher flush + the second-screen `onNoteSaved`): a **clean** model → `adoptDisk` + a `reloadVersion` bump that remounts NotePane on the fresh model; a **dirty** model + a genuine external change → the incoming disk is written to a **`<stem>.conflict-<UTCz>.md.txt`** sidecar (via `write_conflict_sidecar` / `gate_create_exclusive`; the `.txt` final extension makes it inert to every `.md`-gated surface — watcher/index/tree — so no clobber loop, no duplicate-`cid_cn`, not in the sidebar) + a non-blocking banner ("Show copy" + dismiss, 15 locales). Local unsaved work is **never** clobbered (`adoptDisk` refuses on dirty). Behind `WATCHER_ADOPT_ENABLED` (a one-line rollback lever, not a safe steady state).
> - **Three hazards the adversarial review caught + closed (the 2026-06-12 corruption class):** (#6) the `{#key}` async teardown could re-stale the freshly-adopted model — closed by a **dedicated refcounted `reseedingPaths` gate** (NOT the shared cascade flag) spanning the remount across `await tick()`, wrapped in try/finally so a throw can never leave a path gated; (#7) **FocusPane** ignores `value` after mount — closed by a `focusReloadVersion` `{#key}` + a `focusReseedSuppress` that gates every FocusPane teardown-write path; and (the class fix) a **merely-VIEWED note spuriously dirtied on teardown** — which silently defeated `adoptDisk` on every background/focus tab and raised phantom sidecars — closed at the source by making **`setBody`'s string path a no-op on identical content** (the keystroke `Text` path stays O(1), Rule 1). Also folded in-pass: the `onNoteSaved` sibling gap (it adopted the model but forgot the `reloadVersion` remount).
> - **`/migration` ran clean, Phases 1–4.** Architect (`docs/PJ-070-Watcher-External-Change-Adopt-Architect.md`, WA#5 prior art — VS Code/IntelliJ/Sublime all do "reload-if-clean, keep-both-if-dirty"; Obsidian NOT reloading is the documented data-loss cautionary tale = our exact bug), Plan (`…-Plan.md`), Build (§1–§6), 3-agent Audit (all 11 invariants + the class-fix invariant HOLD; 2 low hardenings applied). Per-build diff-scoped safety-inspection + the per-cycle whole-app sweep (`wf_1b7addb3-822`, 38 agents, 15 confirmed — 1 in-diff fixed pre-commit, the rest filed PJ-083→087 + Charter). `/simplify` (4 agents). **svelte-check 0, vitest 334, cargo clean.** Commits `b1a3e388` + `cd5e53fd`. **Boss-validated:** Stage 1 (adopt live, no clobber — disk-verified) + Stage 2 (dirty-conflict → sidecar + banner, both versions preserved).
> - **PJ-072 lead (bonus):** the Boss test pinned the active "Eisa Cognitive Knowledge" universe's on-disk root to **`E:\Cognitive Knowledge\`** (write-journal-confirmed) — distinct from the `E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\` folder that also exists. The diagnostic build is still wanted for WHERE that mapping persists, but WHERE the data lives is known.

**Version 3.38 | 2026-07-12**

> **What changed in v3.38** (**MIG-100 — Auto-Restore Tabs on Relaunch: SHIPPED + Boss-validated across 3 test rounds + migration CLOSED. Closing Constellation no longer forgets the desk — open tabs, the active tab, and the split come back at launch, per-Universe, default-ON, 15 languages. The Phase-4 close audit PASSED (7/7 invariants hold, 6/6 migration-path scenarios clean); 3 deferred-cid lifecycle leaks it found were fixed before close. Ten pre-existing app-killer-class defects were fixed in passing.** Ultracode):
> - **Boss-validated end-to-end (3 rounds).** Stage 1 passed first try. Stage 2 surfaced two real bugs — a **ghost tab** (a moved-while-closed note resurrected from the write-ahead crash buffer) and **cross-universe contamination** (switching to a new universe restored the previous universe’s tabs into it) — both fixed Reproduce-First (RED→GREEN). The contamination fix’s own universe-switch then raised **“Couldn’t save” banners**, whose *true* root cause was an **altitude error in write-authorization** (below); fixed and re-validated. All Boss tests green 2026-07-12.
> - **The design (D2, origin-tagged).** A per-Universe `.constellation/session.json` (machine-written, disposable, `.prev` one-generation rotation), delivered in the boot bundle **tagged with its origin universe root** (`BootBundle.session_root`); the restore **refuses any payload whose origin ≠ the universe it is arming for** (normalized compare) and re-reads the correct root — cross-universe contamination is structurally impossible. Frontend `src/lib/libraries/session.ts`: arrangement-only signature (content/cursor/scroll excluded — Rule 8, zero keystroke-path work), 1 s debounce, signature-guarded + serialized persist with dirty-retry, `stopSessionTracking` = cancel-AND-flush + generation token, **carried-tabs one-boot grace** (a transiently-unreadable file survives one boot, a second strike drops). Restore fires post-`boot:hydrated`, fire-and-forget, **journal-proven ZERO `.md` writes** (Editor-Surface Gate #8); crash-recovery net PRESERVED (`resolveNoteContent(preserveNet, requireDisk)`); `ensure_cid_cn` deferred to first user activation. Graceful close = a Rust `CloseRequested` handshake (`prevent_close` → `session:final-flush` → ack or 700 ms → destroy).
> - **The real switch-flush fix — write-authorization is universe-MEMBERSHIP, not the active pointer.** `write_note`’s `validate_path_in_any_library` authorized writes against only the **active** universe’s libraries; a note in universe A saving to A’s own file is *always* legitimate (the active pointer is navigation, not permission), so a departing tab’s deferred teardown flush — landing a heartbeat after the switch flipped — was refused. Now it falls back — **only on the rare active-miss, so the common save pays nothing** — to every REGISTERED universe’s root + its **OWN** libraries (`own_libraries_for_root`, non-recursive, respecting the federated-write-blocker; never writes through a read-only cUniverse view). A path outside every registered/federated universe is still rejected (security bound intact — the close audit confirmed the widening does NOT re-open contamination).
> - **Phase-4 close audit PASSED** (`wf_c2960e95-207`): all **7 invariants HOLD** (boot/typing/IPC unregressed; relaunch writes zero `.md`; workspaces.json untouched by the auto path; no keystroke/boot-empty write; A’s session can’t reach B’s file; content durability untouched; SS closed at boot) and all **6 migration-path scenarios PASS** (no-session blank boot, rollback-inert stale file, schema/corrupt/carried drift, session_root normalization, cUniverse write, mid-restore crash-sentinel). Its **drift check found 3 deferred-cid lifecycle leaks** (LL-023 class — the pending-set + activation watchers surviving a universe switch, a closed pending tab wedging the auto-unsubscribe, `startSessionTracking` not cancelling a stray deferred-arm) — **all fixed before close** with regressions R15/R16. Final: vitest **318/318**, cargo **1047**, svelte-check **0**.
> - **Ten pre-existing app-killer-class defects fixed in passing (WA#6).** The migration’s cycle-boundary whole-app sweep (`wf_127a517c-479`, 87 agents, 63 confirmed) promoted 2 pre-existing APP-KILLERs to the register (watcher external-change never adopts into the note model → next-keystroke clobber; bulk Accept-All unlocked RMW race). The 3 diff-scoped inspections fixed **all** their in-diff findings before commit and, crucially, closed **4 G6-class defects** the write-auth inspection surfaced — non-atomic `fs::write` on live `universe.json`/`libraries.json` that a crash could truncate into a silent library/federation wipe (now `atomic_write` + a logged best-effort helper).
> - **Docs:** User Manual §3 “Your tabs come back on relaunch” + all 14 translations; the Editing-and-Formatting help topic; scope honesty everywhere (split-pane tab assignment NOT restored — named workspaces never persisted it either; second screen OUT, always starts closed). Toggle-off deletes the stored session (“stop remembering”).
> - **OPEN INVESTIGATION (filed in the Charter, does NOT block MIG-100):** the Boss’s instance boots universes (“Eisa Cognitive Knowledge” 7,751 notes, “Scratch”) that appear in NO on-disk registry findable on the machine, while the shared write-journal records both. Where that instance persists its universe registry is UNKNOWN — needs a diagnostic build logging the resolved `app_data_dir` + registry path at boot.

**Version 3.36 | 2026-07-11**

> **What changed in v3.36** (**The second-screen note-graph is now a complete THREE-lens set — Butterfly, Ledger, Orrery — all on one chassis, one palette shared with the whole app, and correct in 15 languages including RTL. The Orrery (time & aliveness) is the new lens; the palette was unified on the Link Types registry; a run of RTL / Arabic-plural / label-collision fixes landed.** Ultracode):
> - **THE ORRERY — the third lens (time & aliveness).** Answers the one question the Butterfly (composition) and the Ledger (magnitude) cannot: *which of this note’s links are still ALIVE vs going COLD, and is any load-bearing link quietly decaying?* A central **sun** = the note; **six concentric recency orbits** (today → never-walked, `recencyShell()` off `lastTraversed`; `traversalCount==0` pins to the NEVER rim); **angular sector = link type**, and each **wing’s width ∝ its link count**; **direction** = solid disc (outgoing) vs hollow ring (backlink); **size** = `earnedWeight()`; **halo** = confidence (ring style); **warmth** = recency; the **going-cold ALARM** = a status-coloured pulsing ring on a load-bearing link stranded on a cold orbit. **Hover a wing → a real zoom-in:** it grows to ~0.92 of the circle, its dots ENLARGE, and every one of its nodes shows (no `+N`); the resting state stays compact with `+N` clusters. All ~958 links represented, no cap; deterministic even-division within cells (zero jitter, Form-Aligns-to-Purpose). File `NoteOrreryGraph.svelte`; helpers `recencyShell()` / `earnedWeight()` + `RECENCY_SHELLS` in `cockpitGraphData.ts`; registry `orrery` built:true.
> - **Concept-before-function, honestly applied.** Heartwood was **CUT** by the Art-Director concept review (its tree-ring angle encoded nothing — a Form-Aligns-to-Purpose fail; honest form collapsed to a redundant time-strip that the note’s own stage/maturity badges already imply). The Orrery was **REWORKED**, not shipped as drawn: the naive orbital disc was dishonest (inverse space, free angle, lost direction); the team made every degree of freedom carry data. Boss chose to keep the orbital metaphor over a cartesian “Decay Timeline”. Method throughout: multi-agent Art-Director workflows (specialists → AD spec → N competing engineers → adversarial judges → lead-engineer merge), the standing arrangement that the **Art Director & Team own UX/UI design AND coding**.
> - **Palette unified on the Link Types registry (registry base + Style-Setter override).** The lenses had invented a SECOND palette for the same 8 relationships (a `supports` wedge was green while its pill was blue). Now `relColor(id) = var(--rel-<id>, linkTypeColor(id))` — recolouring the vocabulary in the Link Types editor moves the pills, Sight, CCS, GraphMind AND all three lenses together; a Style-Setter **“Note graph → Relationship colours”** category overrides the graph alone (full-centre-zone Butterfly-mimic preview). Fixed in the same pass: **custom link types** now keep their own name+colour (were collapsed to grey “associative”); the **second screen loads the registry** itself (per-window cache; a `link-types:changed` broadcast repaints it live); the **gauge deck** stopped borrowing link colours for confidence/review (uses the shared `--confidence-*` / `--text-status` vars).
> - **The lens toggle lives ON the cockpit page** (moved from Settings). The SS never writes settings (Display-not-Domain): it emits `screen:set-lens`, MAIN performs the `updateSettings` write and its broadcast re-renders the SS — avoiding a real silent-revert bug (main’s `appSettings` isn’t refreshed by SS writes). The dead **“Peek” dial** (resolved to the same note as Follow, consumed nowhere) was removed — `DialMode = normal | locked` (Follow / Pin).
> - **Language-First fixes (15 locales).** The whole `cockpit.*` block (60 strings) was localized ar/de/es/fa/fr/he/hi/ja/ko/pt/ru/tr/ur/zh (mine-first: reused the app’s own wording for 17/22 deck terms; caught that `origin`/`provenance`/`source` collapse to one word in 9 languages and split them — ar `المنشأ / الإسناد / المصدر`). **RTL label-flip fixed:** the graph SVGs are pinned `direction:ltr` (SVG `text-anchor` resolves against inline base direction, so under RTL every label flew off-canvas); type names localize via `relLabelIn($locale)`; the note-box count reads count-then-word in RTL (`212 رابط`). **Butterfly label lane** reserved + wings pulled in (labels no longer clip). **Facet tabs** localized by reusing existing panel keys. **Arabic plural** “many” (11–99) now uses the plain singular not the accusative tanwin (`212 رابط`, not `رابطًا`) across 14 masculine count-nouns — matching the status-bar convention. Orrery recency labels localized (long/short) ×15.
> - **Lens set is now the sharp three:** **Butterfly** (composition — in/out + type mix) · **Ledger** (magnitude — exact comparable counts) · **Orrery** (time — alive vs dormant + the going-cold alarm). Each owns one distinct axis; Heartwood cut. All Boss-validated.

> - **The Butterfly (default, Boss-validated "Pass" 2026-07-10).** Two mirrored wings across a central spine — backlinks left, outgoing right. **Greedy centre-out composition:** each wing sorts its types by count desc, puts the LARGEST on its own horizontal axis (phi=0), then adds each next to whichever side holds the smaller cumulative angular width — so each wing visual mass lands ON the axis and the figure can never read tilted or pinwheeled. **ONE isotropic radius R** — every arc is a true circle; the wide (~2.5:1) stage is filled by an **adaptive vertical envelope** (`R = min(horizReach, vertRoom / max(f*sin(|phi|+w/2)))`), *composition, never scaling* (Boss: "Don't try to stretch it"). Solid wedges (0.85 fill + crisp edge). **Every link is ONE radial stem** from a hub collar out to *its own wedge* rim, ending in a bead; one density scalar `s = rimArc / n` drives stem width, stem opacity, and bead radius, so a 394-stem wedge thins to a legible fan (~34% ink) while a 1-link wedge renders bold. **Earned weight** (`0.55*tierW + 0.45*traversalNorm`) was re-homed from stem LENGTH (now constant) onto **bead radius + stem opacity** — stated plainly rather than left as a dead visual. Type names live in per-wing **edge-lane callout columns** on a strict >=17px ladder, which makes overlap *geometrically impossible* for any text width or locale. Dotted seam `var(--text-normal)` at 0.7.
> - **The Ledger (Boss-approved unchanged).** The balance sheet: a hard central rail, one canonical row per relationship type identical on both sides, backlink bars growing left and outgoing right against a shared scale + ticks, so the in-vs-out asymmetry reads as unequal column mass. Click a bar to open a drawer of that type individual links; click one and the MAIN window navigates. No radial geometry: it cannot be mistaken for a disc.

> - **Boss test PASS ×2:** Stage 1 (the collision recipe — edit → wikilink hop ×4) = instant, app alive. Stage 2 (search typing + Review actions inside the busy window) = keystrokes instant, results match the final query, no freeze anywhere.
> - **Batch 2 — DEFERRED EXPLICITLY (not silently):** every command that **writes note files** — `rename_item`/`move_item`/`delete_item`/`delete_path`/`update_links_on_rename`, `toggle_task`, `update_note_property`, `resolve_structural_conflict`, `constellation_link_set_confidence`/`archive`/`unarchive`, sources/CECE accepts, `set_active_universe` — sync→async changes their ordering vs the debounced save = **content-integrity territory (BUG-023 / Editor-Surface Gate)** → own gated pass with the reproduction harness. > **What changed in v3.16** (**PJ-065 — the Structural / Parent-TOC link type: DESIGNED via the four-phase `/migration`, BUILT, and Boss-validated end-to-end. Plus two fixes the work surfaced — the app-wide 24 s rename slowdown and a latent Sight bug — both fixed.** Ultracode):
> - **Concept (the horse).** A note's place in a *composition* — Book → Part → Chapter → Scene — is **structural**, not cognitive. It answers "where does this sit in the whole work?", not "how does this idea relate to that one?" So PJ-065 adds a **new, NON-cognitive link kind** — the *compositional spine* — that is **excluded from every cognitive surface** (maturity, strata, 360, centrality, tension, health, Sky, aggregates, search grammar, the GraphMind colour map). It is **not** a 9th cognitive type; the 8 cognitive types (+`associative`) are untouched.
> - **Two link types, authored in frontmatter as quoted wikilinks.** `parent:` (child → its one parent) and `contains:` (parent → ordered child list, carries a nullable `seq`). Both authored as `"[[Target Name]]"` under those YAML keys (decision **D3** — wikilink form means they ride the **existing whole-file rename cascade**, so they are rename-safe by construction; no separate maintenance path). Stored in `note_links` with `link_type IN ('parent','contains')` + the new nullable `note_links.seq`.
> - **Read-time resolution (no derived table, no boot walk — LL-022-safe).** Single-parent: a child's own `parent:` wins; ties broken by smallest path; a `contains:` claim that contradicts the child's own parent is **overruled** (strict tree). Acyclicity via a visited-set cycle guard. Both computed lazily in `structural.rs` when the panel opens.
> - **The Structure panel (`StructuralOutlinePanel.svelte`).** Shows the **whole work** (root resolved from `ancestors[0]`), not just a breadcrumb, with a **focus toggle** (whole-work ⇄ this-subtree), a *you-are-here* highlight, and a clamped tooltip. Boss: *"YES! This is more like it… You got what's in my mind and more."*
> - **Guards + one-click resolve (Boss-chosen "strict tree + conflict flag").** A contested child (its own `parent:` says X, but Y's `contains:` also claims it) renders as a two-line row with **Keep** (keep the child's declared parent) / **Move here** (accept the claimant) buttons → `resolve_structural_conflict` edits the one frontmatter field via the proven `gate_write → reindex → cascade:rewrote` path (6 unit tests). Boss validated both actions.
> - **PropertyEditor authoring (Boss directive).** `parent` and `contains` are **preset property choices**; both author as **`list` chips** with bracket-guarded auto-wrap — a user who types `Owner A` (no brackets) gets `[[Owner A]]` stored, with no triple-bracket artefacts. (Arc: link-type auto-wrap double-wrapped → Boss suggested `list` type → fixed.)
> - **Phase-4 audit (3 agents) + fixes.** Exclusion confirmed correct on every user-visible surface; **2 P1 leaks closed** — `sky_backfill.rs` INSERT and `search.rs::extract_wikilinks` (frontmatter structural keys) both now apply `structural_not_in_clause` / skip structural-keyed frontmatter — plus P3 hardening (GraphMind colour map → `cognitiveLinkTypes()`) and a comment sweep.
> - **Bonus fix #1 — the 24 s rename (felt app-wide).** Root cause: a **dead `UPDATE note_links SET target_path = …` in `rename_item`** — `target_path` is **NULL on every row by design** (vestigial; link targets are resolved by `target_name`), so the UPDATE was a full table scan over 234 k rows for zero benefit. **Deleted → rename is instant.** (Mis-diagnosed twice by static reasoning before per-step instrumentation pinned it — Reproduce-First.)
> - **Bonus fix #2 — latent Sight bug (`sight_v6.rs`).** 6 production subqueries (`link_in_count`, contested-EXISTS) + the link-set SELECT matched the inbound side by the always-NULL `target_path`, so they returned 0 / empty whenever Sight v6 is re-enabled. Migrated to match by **`(target_path OR target_name_lower)`** (the established `COALESCE(target_path, target_name)` fallback). Verified live: "ISBN (identifier)" inbound **0 → 5359**. Pre-existing bug; Sight is a disabled Wing → no live impact, no rebuild needed.
> - **Style Setter — "Tab left offset" control** (Boss "Pass"): a range slider on the `cTabs` element drives `--tab-bar-offset` (the tab-bar `padding-inline-start`).
> - **Rollback caveat (P2).** PJ-065's schema delta is **purely additive and inert without the feature**: the `note_links.seq` column is nullable; the `parent`/`contains` registry seeds and the frontmatter `[[ ]]` values are ordinary YAML/rows that the cognitive engine already **excludes**. To roll back, drop the two registry types — the structural `note_links` rows and frontmatter keys can be left in place harmlessly (they contribute to nothing cognitive) or swept with `link_type IN ('parent','contains')`. No data migration is required to disable.
> - **Canonical facts (update mental model):** (a) structural links are a **separate kind** — gate exclusion via `link_types::structural_not_in_clause(col)` / `is_structural_type` / `STRUCTURAL_SEED_IDS = ['parent','contains']`; (b) they are **rename-safe via the whole-file `[[ ]]` cascade** (D3), not a bespoke path; (c) `note_links.target_path` is **NULL on every row** — *never* match link targets by it; resolve by `target_name` / `target_name_lower` (reinforces the PJ-066 "no `COALESCE(col,expr)` in a WHERE" rule); (d) the Structure panel reads **lazily at panel-open** (`structural.rs`), no derived table.

> *Below: the v3.15 preamble, retained for diff visibility.*

> **What changed in v3.15** (**Item 7 — PJ-066 connect-freeze: the felt freeze when connecting a link on a link-dense note ROOT-CAUSED + fixed + Boss-validated ("instant, no freeze at all"). Backlog item 7 of 7 — FINAL; the 7-item Boss backlog is COMPLETE.** Ultracode):
> - **Reproduce-First (5 instrumented measurement rounds)** on the heaviest note (Ancient history, 533 links). The filed "~3 s residual" framing was wrong by an order of magnitude — a single connect froze the app **~47 s**. The diagnosis refuted *two* prior hypotheses (writer-lock-read, frontend-re-render) **and** a mid-session "reindex storm" hypothesis (the caller-tagged trace proved **one connect = exactly one reindex**; the "7 reindexes" seen earlier were the Boss clicking connect *during* the freeze). The lesson: instrument → reproduce → read the trace; never fix on a plausible mechanism.
> - **Four root causes, four surgical fixes** (no schema change, no `/migration` — all additive/behaviour-identical):
>   - **#1 `constellation_embed_notes` was SYNC** → the e5 ONNX inference (~32 s on this note) ran on the single IPC dispatch thread and froze the whole app on every save. → **`#[tauri::command(async)]`** (the sibling of the §C1 reindex-async fix, which had been missed).
>   - **#2 redundant re-embed on a frontmatter-only connect** — a typed-link connect only adds a YAML property (body unchanged) yet re-embedded the whole body. → `saveTabContent(…, bodyUnchanged=true)` → **`force:false`** skips the re-embed when the note is already embedded.
>   - **#4 THE dominant cost — a hidden full-table scan.** `resolve_incoming_target_paths` (the save-path backlink/sky maintenance, run by `maintain_incoming_after_save` + `sky_affected_paths`) resolved a target name via `WHERE COALESCE(name_lower, LOWER(name)) = ?` — the **`COALESCE(...)` in the WHERE defeated every index → a full SCAN of `note_meta` that reads the wide `body_text` rows = 22 s warm / 31 s cold for a SINGLE name resolve.** → new covering index **`idx_note_name_lower(name_lower, path)`** + an index-seeking `UNION` rewrite (post-backfill `name_lower = ?` arm UNION the pre-backfill `name_lower IS NULL AND LOWER(name) = ?` fallback — verified identical to the COALESCE over 200 real names): **21,915 ms → 0.06 ms.**
>   - **#3 `scan_unlinked_mentions` was a SYNC command holding the writer `db` lock** → it blocked the IPC thread for the reindex's full duration (the felt freeze even after the reindex went async). → **`#[tauri::command(async)]` + routed through `with_read_conn`** (the read-only WAL reader, §C3) so it never waits on the writer lock; eventual-consistency is correct for a suggestion panel.
> - **Result (Boss-verified, trace-confirmed):** connect is **instant, no freeze at all**. `maintain_incoming` **31,362 ms → 154 ms**; **zero** `[PJ066-SLOW]` IPC-thread blocks; the reindex (11 s cold / 2.5 s warm) is now **entirely background** — no read blocks the UI.
> - **Canonical facts (update mental model):** (a) the save-path name→path resolve seeks **`idx_note_name_lower`** — **never** put `COALESCE(col, expr)` in a WHERE (it kills the index *and* drags the wide `body_text` rows through a scan); (b) `scan_unlinked_mentions` reads via **`with_read_conn`** (read-only WAL), `async`; (c) the general rule this closes: **any multi-second derived-data command must be `#[tauri::command(async)]` and read via `read_db`/`with_read_conn` — never SYNC on the IPC thread holding the writer lock.**
> - **THE 7-ITEM BOSS BACKLOG (order 1-2-5-4-7-6-3) IS COMPLETE.** Items shipped this arc: §D i18n sentence-embeds · §E live properties count · broader i18n sweep (854 strings) · PJ-067 concept (ratified) · **PJ-066 connect-freeze (this)** · StyleSetter labels · PJ-065 concept (ratified).

> **What changed in v3.12** (**PJ-067 — the Living Link Relationship Model v2 CONCEPT PAPER + Boss-RATIFIED; the R4 grammar question wargamed → `problematizes/answers` = its own interrogative family; no code**. Backlog item 4 of 7; Ultracode):
> - **PJ-067 concept RATIFIED (build nothing).** SO #8 cross-check OK (Concept-Paper-first; depends on the shipped MIG-086 fold). Two frontier Workflows + the Living-Link philosophy → the concept paper `docs/concept-papers/PJ-067-Living-Link-Relationship-Model-v2-Concept-Paper.md`.
> - **The model — two layers.** **(A) DIMENSIONS:** make each link type's structural algebra **declarable** (OWL-2 characteristics: symmetry/transitive/inverse/functional/reflexive) → **typed backlinks from both ends** (store one direction, derive the reverse — SKOS), **transitive closure ON READ** (recursive CTE, *never stored* — the LL-XXX rule), `part-of` transitive only *within one* meronymy subtype. **(B) FAMILIES by the Five Acts** (Tension + Synthesis are the thinnest → priority): a **thematic family** (used-for/prerequisite-of/precedes/near = the Connection act); the **Tension** vocabulary (`undermines`/`undercuts` as children of `contradicts`, `qualifies`, the question relations, refutes-via-confidence); the **Synthesis** frontier (analogy `maps-to` + n-ary `co-completes`).
> - **Two load-bearing flags:** **`complements` → `co-completes`/`jointly-constitutes`** (the naming trap — "complementarity" is the lexical *opposite*; and it's *n-ary*); the **n-ary SYNTHESIS NODE** — a new **`SYNTH` note-kind** the N constituents point into, with confidence/weight *on the node* (W3C Pattern 1 + Davidsonian) — **shared infrastructure with analogy's mature form; build once.**
> - **R4 (the grammar ruling) wargamed → RULED FAMILY.** At the Boss's request, three steelman defence papers (FAMILY / NINTH / UNTYPED) + a neutral findings (`docs/concept-papers/PJ-067-R4-Wargame-Question-Relation.md`). **Boss ruling: `problematizes / answers` enters as its own first-class INTERROGATIVE FAMILY** — NOT a 9th cognitive act and NOT left untyped. The canonical **8 (the answer/declaration acts) + the §7 derived order stay FROZEN**; the untyped link stays the default open question; the question gets a typed home as a distinct *mood* (`problematizes` = directed verdict-free doubt; `answers` = resolution-of-a-question). Guardrail: scope `answers` to question-targets; typing is opt-in.
> - **Hierarchies in Constellation — four kinds, one machinery (new cross-reference in BOTH PJ-065 §2.1 and PJ-067 §2):** taxonomy (`generalizes`/`exemplifies` — *the taxonomy link, already shipped*) · meronymy (`part-of`) · lineage (`derives-from`/`supersedes`) — **cognitive** — vs the **structural** compositional outline (PJ-065). They differ in meaning but share closure-on-read + acyclicity + inverse + ordering — *build the primitive once.*
> - **Canonical fact:** the Living Link vocabulary is becoming **multi-family** — the 8 cognitive/answer acts · the structural parent/TOC link (PJ-065) · the proposed thematic family · the ratified **interrogative** family (questions). "The 8 cognitive acts" + the §7 order are **unchanged**. R1/R2/R3/R5/R6 are ruled at the `/migration` Architect (Tension-first).
> - **NEXT (backlog):** item 5 — the **broader i18n remainder** (~382 partial-locale gaps): **TRIAGE FIRST + a Boss scope ruling** before any sweep (much is intentional — CECE bilingual taxonomy [PJ-043], disabled Sight strings, `_comment` keys, philosopher names); then StyleSetter labels (item 6), PJ-066 speed (item 7).

> **What changed in v3.11** (**PJ-065 — the structural (parent/TOC) link-type CONCEPT PAPER produced + Boss-RATIFIED; no code (Concept-Before-Function)**. Backlog item 3 of 7; Ultracode):
> - **PJ-065 concept RATIFIED (build nothing).** SO #8 cross-check confirmed PJ-065 (Boss-conceived 2026-06-24, from the MIG-086 fold discovery) is valid + unblocked (its dependency, the frontmatter fold, shipped). A 4-front grounding Workflow (`wf_240289a1-cdd`: codebase · Breadcrumbs/Tana/Dendron/Logseq/MOC · SKOS/Dublin-Core/schema.org/OWL · Scrivener/Workflowy/screenwriting) + the Living-Link philosophy → the concept paper `docs/concept-papers/PJ-065-Parent-TOC-Link-Type-Concept-Paper.md`.
> - **The horse:** the structural link is the **compositional spine** — it answers *"what is the ordered shape of the work I'm composing?"*, NOT the cognitive *"how do these ideas relate?"*. It is a **distinct kind** from the 8 cognitive acts: **ordered** (a TOC is an ordering), a **tree/DAG** (acyclic), **settled by authorship not inquiry**, and **exempt from the living-link apparatus** (no weight/confidence/decay) and the topology signals. It serves **Externalization** (the act after Conviction: constellation of ideas → composed work) — NOT the cognitive `part-of` (epistemic meronymy). Use case: authors/screenwriters (chapters/scenes/acts), MOC/outline hierarchies.
> - **The pattern (WA#5, all prior art agrees):** assert one direction → derive the reverse write-time; **order = a separate sort-key** (not on the edge); store direct edges, compute closure on read; enforce acyclicity write-time. The one primitive Constellation lacks: **persisted sibling ORDER** on a relationship (`note_links` has no order column; OrgChart reads the filesystem, not links).
> - **Boss ruling: "Approved"** — concept + design direction ratified (multi-parent with one primary spine; MVP = TOC panel + breadcrumb). **The precise NAME + final design decisions are ruled at the `/migration` Architect; build deferred.** PJ-065 status: Open/Deferred → **Concept RATIFIED, /migration-ready.**

> *Below: the v3.03 preamble, retained for diff visibility.*

> **What changed in v3.03** (**MIG-085 §B — a Unicode case-folding bug fixed (accented-title notes were false orphans) + maturity single-sourced across every surface**):
>
> - **The discovery (the headline).** What began as a P3 "make maturity agree across surfaces" tidy-up surfaced a real, multi-surface **correctness bug**, found by measuring on the live 7,660-note universe. SQLite's built-in `LOWER()` folds **ASCII A–Z only**; it leaves accented capitals (É, Î, Ś, Đ, Š) unfolded. Note **names** were matched to wikilink **targets** via SQL `LOWER(name)` while targets were Rust-folded (full Unicode) — so **13 notes whose titles carry a non-ASCII capital** (`Île-de-France` 17 inbound, `Śramaṇa` 26, `Étienne-Jules Marey` 16, `Émilie du Châtelet`, `Đông Sơn culture`, `Abū Ḥanīfa`, …) **failed to match their own inbound links → `incoming_count = 0`**: shown as **false orphans** in the new Reviewer's 🔗 lens, wrong (sapling) Sky maturity/stratum, 0 backlink badge. The FS-scan surfaces (maturity panel, 360 Inspector — Rust-folded) were *correct*, which **inverted** the original "single-source to `incoming_count`" premise (the DB surfaces were the wrong ones). Boss ruling: **fix the accent bug first, then maturity; include NFC.**
> - **§B.0 — Unicode name-fold (the gating fix).** Research-validated (WA#5, 5-source web research) to the field's dominant pattern — **store one Rust-folded key column, match key-to-key** (Lucene index-time fold / Postgres normalized columns; NOT a `ulower()` SQL function — per-connection-registration landmine; NOT ICU — not in rusqlite bundled). `fold_match_key()` = **NFC → full-Unicode lower → NFC** (no Arabic strip — the target side never stripped, so a strip would fold the name side only and break Arabic links). One canonical fold reused by the new `note_meta.name_lower`, `sky_nodes.id`, `parse_link_body` targets, and aliases. Name-side matches → `COALESCE(name_lower, LOWER(name))` (the column's NULL-ness IS the rollout gate — pre-backfill rows keep today's behaviour, no race). A resumable `name_fold_backfill` fills `name_lower`, NFC-re-folds `alias_lower`, and recomputes the accented notes' `incoming_count` + `sky_nodes.id` + maturity/stratum. NFC also closes the cross-device (macOS NFD vs Windows NFC) duplicate-link class.
> - **§B.1 — maturity single-source.** `MATURITY_SQL_EXPR` inbound: `COUNT(*)` → `COUNT(DISTINCT source_path)` and `status='active'` → `status != 'archived'`, so the Sky trigger's maturity **equals `note_meta.incoming_count` by construction**. `maturity.rs` rewritten from a full-filesystem walk to a pure `note_meta` read (a **Rule-8 win** + agreement); `inspector360` overrides `total_inbound` with `incoming_count`. STRATUM's ≥5 inbound-edge signal stays `COUNT(*)` (it must match the FS `strata.rs` the 360 uses — the one place DISTINCT was *not* applied).
> - **§B.2 — outbound single-source (Boss-caught at the Stage-2 test).** The 360 Inspector header showed **↑34** outgoing while Backlinks/`outgoing_count` showed **16** — the FS scan counts raw `[[link]]` occurrences (a Wikipedia import duplicates targets), the canonical count is the **16 distinct active `note_links` edges**. `inspector360` now overrides BOTH `total_inbound` and `total_outbound` from `note_meta.incoming_count`/`outgoing_count` (one `read_connection_counts` read). The 360 header (↑16 ↓17) now matches the Backlinks panel both directions; the type-breakdown bars + dot matrix still visualize every link *instance* (a separate representation, unchanged). **Boss-validated end-to-end (Stages 1 + 2).**
> - **Verified.** `fold_match_key` + cross-surface agreement tests; full Rust suite **969 passed, 0 failed**; svelte-check 0; **live-copy rehearsal on the real universe** — all 13 accented notes 0→correct count, **zero collateral** on the 7,647 ASCII notes, zero false orphans remain. A high-effort code review's **6 findings were all fixed** (none deferred, WA#6): stratum-DISTINCT over-application reverted; maturity status aligned; backfill INNER-JOIN miss re-keyed; maturity scope trailing-separator trim; `alias_lower` NFC re-fold; `getBacklinks` JS NFC.
> - **Doc:** `docs/MIG-085B-Architect-Plan-Unicode-Name-Fold.md`. **Approved follow-up still open:** MIG-086 — Tier-2 link suggestions for orphans/fragiles (relatedness via the Index FTS5 co-occurrence, one-click create).

> **What changed in v3.01** (**MIG-083 SHIPPED end-to-end — Review Pulse is now Rule-8 write-time + the new Mode-2 staleness lens, Boss-validated live, triple-reviewed, audited; MIG-080 §F now unblocked**):
>
> - **MIG-083 §A–§E COMPLETE + Boss-validated.** The Review panel that re-walked the whole library filesystem on every open (a Rule-8 violation: `read_dir` recursion + `fs::metadata` per note + `read_to_string`+regex per checkpoint) now reads a **write-time-maintained `review_schedule` SQLite table** — an indexed `SELECT … WHERE due_days <= today` with **zero filesystem access**. Measured on the live **7,660-note** "Eisa Cognitive Knowledge" universe: **get_due_notes 232 ms → ~18 ms**. The legacy `scan_due_recursive` is removed.
> - **Mode-2 "Staleness" — built + Boss-validated live.** A note is flagged **stale** when a **load-bearing OUT-dependency** (`supports`/`contradicts`/`derives-from`/`part-of`/`supersedes`; NOT `associative`) had its **content actually change** (FNV-1a body hash; a touch/sync/frontmatter save does NOT fire) on a later **local** calendar day than the note's last **explicit ✓ review**. A **separate lens** from time-based Due-for-Review (Boss: never merged). Both lenses surface together in `get_due_notes` (each row carries its `reason`; stale rows carry the triggering neighbour/type/date). Resolution via `note_links.target_cid_cn → note_meta.cid_cn`. Boss saw it live: 🥀 on a note whose dependency changed after its review.
> - **Boss rulings this session:** (1) staleness fires on **substantive (plain-body) edits** only — diacritic/formatting-only is a documented fast-follow; (2) the two lenses stay **fully separate** — snooze hides from Due-for-Review (Lens-1) only, a snoozed note can still surface as Stale; (3) a configurable **staleness grace period** Setting (Settings → **Review** → days, min 1, default 1) — a dependency change flags only ≥ grace days after the review (grace=1 = strict next-day). Localized ×15.
> - **Process:** §D went through the §D/§E adversarial pattern — a **24-finding review** + a **4-agent re-verify** + the **`/migration` Phase-4 audit** (invariants/drift/migration-path). Every confirmed finding FIXED (none deferred, WA#6): the P1 mtime-fallback false-fire (→ baseline `content_hash` + require `content_changed_at IS NOT NULL`); snooze-lost-on-reindex + sibling-library bleed + UTC/local day skew + self-links + malformed-date + non-deterministic tie-break; a NEW rename-phantom regression (→ migrate the row + INNER-JOIN guard); and the **missing reconcile self-heal** (`review::recompute_all_in`, now mirroring `tag_counts`). A **live-copy rehearsal harness** (`review_rehearse.rs`) proves on the real corpus: parity vs an independent reference, touch-test 0, <100 ms, Mode-2 fires.
> - **MIG-080 §F now UNBLOCKED** — the note-context **Review tab** (`get_note_review_status`, O(1)) + the full-page **two-lens reviewer** over the now-cheap read. Then §G closes MIG-080. (`record_note_visit→openNoteTab` stays dropped: opening ≠ review.)

> **What changed in v3.00** (**a marathon session: MIG-080 §B–§E shipped (note-context right-rail splits) + TWO new top-principals + MIG-083 opened (Review Pulse Rule-8 redesign) — architected, planned, §A + §B-1 built, and a NEW research-validated feature concept (change-triggered staleness) defined**):
>
> - **MIG-080 §B–§E COMPLETE + Boss-validated** — the right sidebar is now note-context: §B Tags (note-scoped) · §C Tasks (left-dock agenda + theming + Style-Setter + NL dates) · §D Source Review split (note-rail vs Cataloger) · §E Knowledge Health split (note's tensions vs universe dashboard). **§D + §E were each hardened by adversarial-review passes that caught 17 real defects before the Boss tests — two genuinely dangerous** (a universe-wide "Reject all" one click from a single note's card; a correctness bug + a stale-status flash in §E). All fixed, none deferred. (§F now BLOCKED on MIG-083; §G remains.)
> - **TWO new top-principals (CLAUDE.md + memory):** **Concept Before Function — the Horse and the Carriage** ("a function without a concept is a carriage with no horse — state the concept first"); **Fix What You Discover** (Working Agreement #6 — "if a review surfaces it, fix it in the same pass; no documented-but-unfixed defects").
> - **MIG-083 — Review Pulse → Rule-8 write-time schedule (IN PROGRESS).** Concept-before-function caught that §F's full-page reviewer would be built on `get_due_notes`, a Rule-8 violation (full-FS-walk + content read of every `.md` per open). Boss ruled fix Rule 8 first → MIG-083. **Architected** + **Planned** (`docs/MIG-083-Architect-*.md`, `docs/MIG-083-Plan.md`; 5 phases, Boss-approved): a derived `review_schedule` table maintained write-time in `index_note` (the `tag_counts` pattern), gated on `schema_versions.review`, resumable back-fill; reads become `SELECT WHERE due_days<=today`. **Built: §A** (inert table + corrected pure logic: 1·3·7·14·30 ladder, `tags_json` checkpoint, staleness trigger-types; `c30431e6`) **+ §B-1** (gated DB-maintenance fns + corrected `mark_reviewed` + `record_note_visit` removed; `73a79745`). **18 review unit tests pass; everything INERT (gated off until §C).**
> - **NEW feature concept — Mode 2 "Staleness" (defined + WA#5-validated; concept paper §12):** a note is STALE when a **load-bearing OUT-dependency** (`supports`/`contradicts`/`derives-from`/`part-of`/`supersedes`; NOT `associative`) had its **content change** after its last **explicit ✓ review**; all maturities; 1-hop; a **separate lens** from time-based review. It's the **Truth-Maintenance-System / changed-dependency-invalidation** pattern applied to typed Living Links — **novel in PKM** (no SR tool triggers on a neighbour changing; literal analog: dosu.dev's "Git Age Delta"). Research caught the first predicate would over-fire → scoped to out-deps/load-bearing/content-hash/1-hop. (`record_note_visit→openNoteTab` §F wiring dropped: opening ≠ review.)
> - **NEXT (resume here): MIG-083 §B-2** — the `index_note`/`reindex_delete` hot-path hooks + the action-writer row-sync. Then §C (back-fill+stamp) → §D (read swap + staleness JOIN + harness + Boss test) → §E (cleanup+audit) → MIG-080 §F → §G. **Open §B-2 sub-questions:** the `sky_nodes.stratum` TEXT format to parse for real stratum; the action writers need `app.state::<SearchState>` DB access to sync the row; `content_changed_at` (Mode-2 signal) best folded into §D where the staleness JOIN lives.

> **What changed in v2.99** (**MIG-080 §E COMPLETE — Knowledge Health split into note-context (right-rail) vs universe (KH Dashboard); 17 findings across THREE adversarial review passes, ALL fixed; + TWO new top-principals canonised**):
>
> - **§E — Knowledge Health split.** *Concept (the horse):* the right-rail Health tab answers **"what is unhealthy about THIS note?"** (contradicted / orphaned / single-point-of-failure / in a structural gap); the universe `KnowledgeHealthDashboard` (full-page) stays whole. **Option B architecture** (chosen after the review exposed the plan's server-side per-note filter as wrong-shaped): `detect_tensions` runs ONCE per library (cached), and `tensionReport` is a **`$derived` client-side slice** (`filterTensionsForNote`) — no per-note-switch recompute (Rule 8). `GapItem.member_names` (full, for correct gap membership); contradictions emit **BOTH perspectives** (source "contradicts X" + target "contradicted by Y" — a contradicted note isn't healthy); a new O(1) `note_tension_status` IPC drives **honest states** ("not analyzed yet" / "shares its title — can't reliably assess") instead of a false ✓; `screen:note-saved` **debounced refresh**; tension **details localized ×15** (`detail_kind`+`detail_args`). 9 new tension tests/strings; 2 new Rust unit tests.
> - **THREE adversarial review passes, 17 findings, ALL fixed (zero deferred).** §E-base (10, incl. the gap-truncation correctness bug + the per-note recompute) → fix-pass-2 (7, incl. a stale-status FLASH that would have defeated the honesty gate, + a Rule-8 re-detect on every autosave). This is the canonical arc behind the new "Fix what you discover" principle.
> - **TWO new top-principals (CLAUDE.md + memory):**
>   - **Concept Before Function — the Horse and the Carriage** *(Architecture Principles)*: state a function's clear, sound CONCEPT (its purpose) before building it; "a function without a concept is a carriage without a horse." Precedes Constraint-as-Design + Form-Aligns-To-Purpose in time. Operationalised by the concept-paper-per-function bring-up method.
>   - **Fix What You Discover** *(Working Agreement #6)*: if a review/audit surfaces it — any severity — fix it in the same pass; no documented-but-unfixed defects.
> - **NEXT — §F (Review Pulse split)** → §G (final reconcile + audit + /simplify).

**Version 2.89 | 2026-06-17**

> **What changed in v2.89** (**MIG-079 §C.2d — SHIPPED + Boss-validated: the Sky read is deferred off boot; cold `graph_ready` ~11 s → ~1.5 s, a ~7× boot win**):
>
> - **The remaining boot stall WAS the Sky read — confirmed by measurement, then removed.** Post-§C.2c the app was responsive at `hydrated≈1.1 s`, but cold `graph_ready≈11 s` was almost entirely **queue wait**: the graph IPC sat behind the synchronous `cache_boot_snapshot_sky`, which reads the **233,995-row `sky_links`** table cold. The IPC arrival trace nailed it — an **11,374 ms gap with NO other IPC dispatched** (a sync command monopolising the single IPC thread); the same read warm is **250 ms**, so the 11.4 s is purely cold disk I/O.
> - **The fix (Boss-approved Option B+): defer the Sky read off boot + async-ify + warm-up.** (1) `cache_boot_snapshot_sky` is now `#[tauri::command(async)]` (the §9.1 lever — runs on Tauri's worker pool, never monopolises the IPC thread). (2) The boot `loadGraph` no longer reads sky; `graphReady` fires on the graph (tags+aliases) payload only. (3) Sky View / CNS / Lens / Sight load the graph lazily on **first open** via a memoised `ensureSky()` (mirrors `ensureFullLinks`), gated by a new `skyEverOpened` flag (the LL-022 lazy-mount pattern). (4) An **after-idle background warm-up** (`schedule(() => ensureSky())` after `boot:graph-ready`) pre-loads sky on the worker thread so the first open is usually instant. Guards: `_skyEpoch` (universe-switch staleness) + `_skyGeneration` (same-epoch double-load from a `federation:ready` force). New `skyReady` flag; the Sky View spinner now gates on `!skyReady` (reuses the existing `layout.skyViewLoading` string — **zero new i18n**). `handleUniverseSwitch` now resets sky state (closes a pre-existing latent stale-sky race — `skyNodes` was never reset on switch).
> - **MEASURED (cold boot via PC restart, boot-history `[22]`): `graph_ready` 11,000–11,300 ms → 1,555 ms; queue 9,500–9,700 ms → 178 ms; `hydrated` unchanged (~1.3 s).** Boss: Sky View opened **instantly** (warm-up beat the open). Stage-2 PASS: notes untouched (Editor-Surface Gate), Lens shows real clusters, universe-switch shows the right graph in both universes.
> - **Option C ruled out (the handover's open question, answered):** "render nodes-at-boot, stream edges later" is NOT viable — the d3-force/PIXI engine needs all edges at init (no windowing/LOD). Edges + nodes load together on open. **WA#5:** defer-to-open is the Obsidian-v1.7.2 *DeferredView* / lazy-bootstrap standard; eager-full-graph-at-boot is the documented anti-pattern (Logseq/Obsidian freeze on large vaults).
> - **Migration rigor:** Architect (`docs/MIG-079-C2d-Architect-Defer-Sky-Read.md`, 4 mapping agents) → Plan (`docs/MIG-079-C2d-Plan.md`) → Boss-approved Option B+ → Build (§C.2d-1 `23fdd45f`, §C.2d-2 `cff8f827`) → **Audit (4 agents) BEFORE the Boss test**: all 8 invariants + 5 migration scenarios PASS; **two fixes applied** — P1 double-write race (the `_skyGeneration` guard) and P2 Lens-computes-on-empty-sky (`toggleLens` awaits `ensureSky()` first). `/simplify`: diff clean; 3 optional micro-refactors deferred to protect the validated binary. svelte-check 0; `cargo test --lib` 936/0.
> - **Boot-perf note:** the Sky read joins `note_links` (§C.2b) as a deferred-off-boot read; the only 234k cold read remaining at boot is now GONE. The boot pipeline (§15.2) reads core (notes/libs/settings) + graph (tags/aliases) only; sky + full edges are lazy.

The boot graph read (`cache::read_tags`, a 5.6 s full-`tags_json` scan every launch — a CLAUDE.md Rule-8 read-time recompute) is replaced by a persisted summary kept current write-time: `index_note` and `reindex_delete_note` apply a per-tag **±delta** (`new − old`) inside their existing transaction, gated on `schema_versions.tag_counts`; `read_tags_in_schema` reads `{schema}.tag_counts WHERE n>0` when stamped, **else falls back to the legacy live scan** (zero-risk); `reconcile_filesystem` rebuilds it authoritatively (self-heal). Boot `read_tags` 5.6 s → ~ms (from the 2nd boot after ship).
> - **Backfill = ONE atomic `json_each` aggregate** (refinement of the handover's "batched, like `note_body_backfill`"). A counter is an *additive* aggregate, so a batched build racing live ±deltas would double-count — the exact race flagged as audit item (b). Building **and** stamping inside ONE `IMMEDIATE` transaction (dedicated connection, the proven reconcile-`walk_conn` pattern) **eliminates** the race: a concurrent save serializes either before the backfill (its delta gated-off; the aggregate sees its note_meta) or after (table stamped; its delta applies) — both converge (proof-by-cases in the session log). Tags have no 128 MB-row problem, so one statement is cheap; the ~6 s lock hold is one-time, background, post-paint, and WAL keeps boot READS unblocked.
> - **Reproduce-First on the data shape:** all 7,653 `tags_json` rows are clean string-arrays (0 NULL/malformed/non-array/non-string/empty/dup); `serde` and `json_each` aggregates are byte-identical (19,542 distinct / 36,193 occ); the 5.6 s is SQLite's wide-row traversal (inline `body_text`), not JSON parsing — the ~19.5k-row summary reads in ms.

> **What changed in v2.78** (**The Delete-path fix — the "Deleted files" setting now GOVERNS deletion (was a silent no-op); deletes are always recoverable; "Permanently delete" dropped — SHIPPED + Boss-validated**):
>
> - **The data-loss gap closed.** `delete_item` ALWAYS hard-deleted regardless of Settings → Universe & Libraries → "Deleted files" (`// For now, always permanent delete`) — the dropdown was a no-op, so users expecting the Recycle Bin (the default) or who chose ".trash folder" for safety were **silently losing data permanently**. New Rust **`delete_path(app, path, mode, trash_root)`** (`libraries.rs`) routes by the setting: **permanent** → remove · **trash** → move into `<trash_root>/.trash` (de-colliding like `move_to_trash`; cross-volume-safe rename→copy+remove + recursive dir copy) · **system** → OS Recycle Bin (the new **`trash` crate**). All modes `reindex_delete_note`; `.trash` is already excluded from walks+index (`file_kinds.rs` EXCLUDED_DIRS / `embeds.rs` IGNORED_DIRS) so trashed notes vanish from tree+search. One shared frontend **`deleteWithSetting(path)`** (store.ts) resolves the `.trash` root and replaces the hard-coded delete at BOTH real sites (`handleDeleteConfirm` + `handleBatchDelete`).
> - **".trash folder" scope choice (Boss extension).** A sub-option under the dropdown: **within the note's library** OR **at the universe root** (`trashFolderScope: 'library' | 'universe'`). For Eisa's layout the universe-root case is a cross-folder-tree move (libraries under `E:\Cognitive Knowledge\…`, universe root under `E:\Constellation Universes\…`) — handled cross-volume-safe. i18n `settings.files.{trashFolderScope,scopeLibrary,scopeUniverse}` ×15.
> - **"Permanently delete" dropped (Boss ruling — *"who would choose Permanently deleted? I wouldn't"*).** Cross-check: Obsidian offers it, but macOS/Windows file managers have NO global always-permanent mode (permanent is an explicit one-off). For Constellation's protect-your-knowledge ethos the global option is a footgun. The dropdown is now **System trash / .trash folder** (both recoverable); `deleteWithSetting` + `applyParsedSettings` migrate any legacy 'permanent' → 'system'. The engine KEEPS a `permanent` mode in `delete_path` for a FUTURE *explicit* "Delete permanently" action — never a silent global mode.
> - **Boss-validated Stage 1 + Stage 2, all destinations disk-confirmed** (Working Agreement #1): library `.trash` · universe `.trash` (the cross-tree move) · Windows Recycle Bin (verified via Shell.Application + original-location metadata) · permanent-gone-everywhere · folder delete · List-mode batch. The List-mode batch confirm now states the destination instead of falsely claiming "cannot be undone."
> - **Deferred follow-ups (logged, NOT built):** (1) right-click batch delete in List mode · (2) the native `confirm()` box → Constellation's styled dialog · (3) **comprehensive app-wide right-click** (a real initiative — inventory + plan, not piecemeal) · the **unified Trash view** (Boss-chosen over renaming per-library `.trash`; same-name `.trash` is the standard, disambiguated by location — renaming would break the exact-name exclusion + Obsidian trash recognition) · an **explicit "Delete permanently"** action.
> - **User-facing:** delete now honors the setting + is always recoverable. User Manual (*Notes Management → Deleting notes*) + help (*Notes Management*) updated (EN); help mirror rides the batched-translation debt. New dependency: the `trash` crate.

> **What changed in v2.77** (**MIG-076 §E-2 — the write-integrity diagnostics line — SHIPPED + Boss-validated; §E now CLOSED, only §F remains**):
>
> - **§E-2 ships the Settings → Security & Privacy "Write integrity" readout.** New Rust IPC `read_write_journal_stats` (`write_gate.rs`) streams the `write-journal.jsonl` (+ its one rotated `.old`) and returns `{writes, anomalies, would_refuse_identity/stale, last_anomaly_ts, refused_exists, enforce, exists, rotated, dir}`. **Anomalies = the SHADOW-mode would-refuse verdicts** (`would_refuse_identity` + `would_refuse_stale`) — the count that must be 0 for the §F1 enforcement flip. The Settings line (SettingsModal Security section) shows Writes journaled / Anomalies (✓0 green · ⚠N red + the **most-recent-anomaly date**) / Monitoring (shadow mode) / Open journal folder; **re-reads on every section entry**. i18n `writeIntegrity.*` ×15 (native).
> - **The diagnostic earned its keep on first run.** Reading Eisa's live journal, the readout surfaced **2 anomalies** — both `editor_save` from 2026-06-12 19:57/20:02 carrying a stale `…9E76` cid onto different notes: the exact **§C new-note-while-open identity leak** the journal caught on 06-12 and that was then fixed. Zero new anomalies since, across ~640 writes through the §D + §E-1 testing. The `last_anomaly_ts` field was added precisely so this perpetual-but-historical "⚠ 2" reads correctly as stale (date shown).
> - **The build-process lesson (logged to memory + here).** The first §E-2 binary shipped with the Rust IPC but NO Settings line — because `cargo build --release` (run directly) only recompiles Rust and **re-embeds the existing `../build` frontend**; the SvelteKit bundle is regenerated ONLY by `npm run build` (the tauri.conf `beforeBuildCommand`). Stage-0 "binary newer than source" passed yet the binary held a stale frontend. **Rule: any frontend change → `npm run build` THEN `cargo build --release`, and verify by grepping `build/` for the new string** (binary-mtime alone is insufficient). Memory `feedback_frontend_build_before_cargo`.
> - **Boss iteration (3 rounds, all validated).** Stage 1 PASS (line shows 640 / ⚠2 / June 12, matching the Claude-side disk count). Two follow-ups fixed: the "Most recent" label → **"Most recent anomaly"** (it's the last anomaly, not the last note); the panel now **auto-re-reads on section entry** (the manual Refresh looked dead because the Settings modal blocks editing — no new writes occur while it's open, so there was nothing new to fetch). Then **the Refresh button was dropped entirely** (Boss call — the auto-refresh makes it redundant); its dead i18n key removed ×15.
> - **REMAINING MIG-076 scope:** only **§F** — flip `WRITE_GATE_ENFORCE=true` after a clean soak + the refusal/quarantine/freshness recovery UX + permanent regression suite + 3-agent audit + `/simplify` + close. The WriteGate CAS is still in **shadow mode**.
> - **User-facing:** the Write-integrity readout (new) — User Manual §19 (Security and Privacy) updated (EN); help mirror rides the batched-translation debt.

> **What changed in v2.76** (**MIG-076 §E-1 — the universe-wide name-collision dialog — SHIPPED + Boss-validated (Stage 1 + Stage 2, disk + content confirmed); the trash de-collide fix lands with it**):
>
> - **§E-1 ships the name-collision dialog (PJ-003 §E1b).** Creating a note with a **typed** name, or renaming a note, onto a title that already exists **anywhere in the universe** (every library + every federated child universe) now opens one conventional modal — **Change name / Overwrite / Cancel** (`src/lib/components/CollisionDialog.svelte`, NEW) — instead of create's silent auto-suffix or rename's swallowed "already exists" failure. The check is authoritative: it reuses `resolveWikilinkCrossLibrary` (the SAME resolver the `[[wikilinks]]` use, fed by `resolve_universe_libraries` — federated, so cUniverse duplicates are caught by the same code path). **Overwrite is recoverable** — the displaced note is moved to its library's `.trash` first, never hard-deleted. Quick Capture's auto-named notes are NOT interrupted (a separate Rust path); folders are unaffected (`!isDir`). i18n `collision.*` ×15 (native).
> - **Boss-validated, disk + content proven (Working Agreement #1).** Stage 1 (same-library create — the dialog + all three buttons) + Stage 2 (cross-library create + rename collision + Overwrite-to-trash) both **PASS**. Claude-side disk read confirmed: the renamed note kept **its own** cid + body + **old name preserved as an alias** (so old `[[links]]` still resolve — and collision detection is alias-aware as a bonus); the displaced original sits intact in `.trash`. No identity leak, no corruption — the content-integrity class stays closed through the new surface.
> - **The trash de-collide fix (Obsidian-style, Boss-approved this session).** Stage-2 validation surfaced a real edge: `move_to_trash` reused the exact filename, so trashing a second note sharing a name with one already in `.trash` **atomically replaced — and silently lost — the earlier trashed copy**. Fixed (`src-tauri/src/libraries.rs`): on a `.trash` name clash, suffix the stem with ` {n}` (*Foo 1*, *Foo 2*) — matching Constellation's own create-collision naming. **Never clobber.** Release build green (2m40s).

Both belong with §F's recovery/safety UX. **Trash is per-library by design** (Boss-confirmed): a Library is a portable, self-contained vault (Obsidian convention — `.trash` at the vault root); a universe-root trash would scatter deletions across folder trees (Eisa's libraries live under `E:\Cognitive Knowledge\…`, not the universe root) and break portability.
> - **Scope decision (Eisa, this session): §E = collision dialog (§E-1, done) + diagnostics line (§E-2, next).** The refusal / quarantine / freshness recovery UX folds into **§F**. §E-2 = a journal-read IPC + a Settings → Debug "Write integrity" readout (writes journaled / anomalies count).

The WriteGate CAS is still in **shadow mode**.

> **What changed in v2.75** (**MIG-076 §D — quiesced rename + title-rename re-land — SHIPPED + Boss-validated; the orientation-§13 title-rename gap CLOSED; a 6× rename perf win — the on-save embed lock contention — fixed**):
>
> - **§D ships the rename layer on the §C single-ownership foundation.** Title-rename now runs the SAME full quiesced orchestration as a sidebar rename (freeze → flush-through-model → `rename_item` → wikilink cascade → deliberate remount), so every `[[link]]` to a title-renamed note heals — closing the long-open **orientation-§13 title-rename gap** that the reverted `a086e1ee` had opened. Boss Stage-2 (the exact BUG-023 probe: A links B, rename B by title, inspect both files) **PASS** — both notes keep their own identity, the link heals, **zero write-journal anomalies**. The content-integrity class stays closed through the feature that originally broke it (BUG-023).
> - **The freeze overlay** (`src/lib/components/CascadeFreezeOverlay.svelte`, NEW). A read-only "Updating links…" overlay (localized ×15 — `cascade.updating`) covers every affected-library editor pane during the wikilink cascade, blocking input so no keystroke is lost across the remount. Raised **right after `renameItem`** (the proven-safe post-rename reactive context) and lifted in a `finally`. Reactive signal: the new `cascadeFreeze` store (SEPARATE from the non-reactive `cascadingPaths` write-gate Map — the editor surfaces subscribe to the overlay one; the hot-path save gate stays a plain Map lookup). Mounted on the active / split / index editor panes (each made `position:relative`). Focus is intentionally excluded (a rename can't originate from the sidebar-less, read-only-title Focus surface; §C identity-binding covers Focus content).
> - **The flush-from-model seam fix (§D1).** Under §C the write-ahead buffer is fed only on tab teardown (`NoteEditor.handleFlush`), NOT per keystroke — so `flushAllTabsInLibrary` (the pre-cascade flush) was reading a stale buffer and could leave a freshly-typed link to a just-renamed note broken (a sub-1.5s pre-autosave race, latent in shipped §C). It now composes the flush from the MODEL (the §C authority) under `SINGLE_OWNERSHIP` (`saveNoteSession`, identity-guarded, `isNoteDirty`-gated). One caller (the rename path); legacy WAB path preserved in the `else`.
> - **The 6× rename perf win — the on-save embed lock contention (the headline perf finding).** A rename done right after editing a note used to take ~10.6s. Root cause (read + DB-verified, not guessed): `constellation_embed_notes` (the on-save semantic embed; 8,786 vectors active here) held `search_state.db.lock()` across its WHOLE loop **including the multi-second `run_embedding` model inference**, so the next rename's `reindex_single_note` (`db.lock()`) blocked ~10s behind it. **Fix** (`src-tauri/src/embeddings.rs`): the DB lock is now scoped to only the existence-check + the INSERT — **inference runs lock-free**. Rename-after-edit **10.6s → 1.77s**; a normal rename (no recent edit) is **~400ms**. This is a BROAD win, not rename-only: every save's embed used to freeze the whole search DB during inference. (The earlier handover's "the ~7s rename is the whole-universe wikilink scan" was **imprecise** — the trace proved the cascade scan + the tree refresh are fast; the cost was this lock.) Residual ~1.4s (CPU during concurrent embed inference — not a lock) logged as a follow-up PJ.
> - **Process lesson (logged, this session).** instant-freeze **v1** — raise the freeze BEFORE `renameItem`, keyed by tab.id — **regressed** the cascade + tree refresh (both silently skipped) when an edited tab was open. Could not be pinned by reading (`cascadeFreeze` has only the overlay as a subscriber); per **Reproduce-First + Stop-On-Correction**, secured first (reverted to the Part-A-passing version, Boss-chosen), bisection-confirmed the pre-rename raise as the culprit, then shipped **v2** (raise after). Reproduce-First (the write-journal + a one-shot Boss-readable timing trace) is what overturned the wrong slowness assumption and found the real lock. Harness `tests/mig-076/` stays **28/28** (Recipe H = the title-rename lifecycle).
> - **REMAINING MIG-076 scope:** **§E** refusal/recovery dialog + name-collision dialog (PJ-003 §E1b: Change name / Overwrite-trash-backed / Cancel) + i18n ×15 · **§F** flip `WRITE_GATE_ENFORCE=true` after a clean soak + permanent regression suite + 3-agent audit + `/simplify` + close. The WriteGate CAS is still in **shadow mode**.
> - **User-facing:** title-rename now cascades links (a behavior change — the §13 gap closes) + the freeze overlay (new). Help topic + User Manual updated (EN); the 14 translated help mirrors ride the standing batched-translation debt.

> **What changed in v2.74** (**MIG-076 §C — SINGLE CONTENT OWNERSHIP — SHIPPED + BOSS-VALIDATED (5/5). The content-integrity bug class is structurally closed. `milestone/mig-076-single-ownership` tagged + ZIP-backed.**):
>
> - **The cure, ratified end-state.** After the §CB increments failed (see v2.73), Eisa ruled *"Forget the clean slate. Solve this issue for good. NO more patching."* Three top-principal rules were locked into CLAUDE.md (Reproduce-First; Solve-the-Class-Not-the-Instance; the Editor-Surface Gate Checklist). The fix was then **designed whole, built and proven in isolation, and landed as one validated swap behind a toggle** — exactly as the new rules demand.
> - **The architecture (three new leaf modules in `src/lib/editor/`):**
>   - **`noteModel.ts`** — THE single content authority per open note: `{id, path, cid, props, body: CM6 Text, version, savedVersion}` in a non-reactive module Map. Replaces the three drifting copies (editor text / stale `tab.content` / write-ahead buffer) whose mismatch was the entire disease. **Identity-guarded BOTH directions:** `compose(id, expectPath)` refuses to hand out content for the wrong path (read-out guard); `setBody/setProps(id, …, expectPath)` refuse to accept a write addressing the wrong path (write-in guard). Plus `adoptDisk` (freshness-gated external-change reconciliation), `markSaved`/`isDirty`.
>   - **`noteSession.ts`** — the thin testable glue the components call (`open/ensure/editBody/editProps/seedBody/compose-via-save/repath/externalChange/close`). The §CB bugs lived in glue tangled inside `.svelte` lifecycle; pulling it into a plain module is what made it harness-provable.
>   - **`ownershipFlag.ts`** — `SINGLE_OWNERSHIP` (currently **true**). Instant rollback: flip false + rebuild → proven legacy behavior, no half-state (the legacy path is preserved in the `else` branch of every chokepoint).
> - **Integration (commit `1d93732c` swap, `19ff135b` fix, `4cc77c2a` flag-on).** NoteEditor + FocusPane seed via `seedBody` and save via identity-bound `compose`; FocusPane binds to a **captured focus-session identity** (closes the in-focus-switch cross-write); `saveTabContent` + the store lifecycle (`openNoteTab` reuse/new, `loadTabHistoryEntry`, `renameItem`, `moveItem`, `reloadTabsFromDisk`) drive the model **synchronously** from the explicit note-open event (not the async `ensure` $effect); second-screen `onNoteSaved` adopts freshness-gated. `parseFrontmatter`/`buildFullContent` stayed in `store.ts` (hoisted-fn import cycle is eval-safe).
> - **The one Boss-test failure, found + fixed.** The first swap (flag on) passed Focus + rename visually, but the **write-journal caught a new-note-while-open identity leak** the eye couldn't see: creating a new note reused the tab, and the torn-down PropertyEditor for the *previous* note fired a last save that poisoned the reused model with the old note's identity (§C test's cid landed in §C Eisa No. 2.md). Rolled back to safe on Eisa's order; root cause confirmed from journal+code (not guessed); fixed with the **write-in identity guard + synchronous model-open**; reproduced as harness **Recipe G** (the exact poison) → blocked. Re-test: **5/5 PASS, journal 90 writes / ZERO anomalies, real notes untouched.**
> - **The harness (`tests/mig-076/`, 25/25):** `noteModel.test.ts` (acceptance invariants I1–I5), `runtimeHarness.test.ts` (every failure recipe as a view-vs-disk parity scenario, incl. Recipe G), `currentBugRepro.test.ts` (characterizes the pre-cure defects). Permanent CI surface — this bug class cannot silently return.
> - **Still pre-existing (NOT a regression):** the ~7s rename is the whole-universe cascade wikilink-scan (disk rename itself is ~1ms); **§D's quiesced rename owns that UX.**
> - **REMAINING MIG-076 scope:** **§D** quiesce-rename (freeze+progress overlay for the 7s scan) + title-rename re-land · **§E** refusal/recovery dialog + name-collision dialog (PJ-003 §E1b: Change name / Overwrite-trash-backed / Cancel) + i18n ×15 · **§F** flip `WRITE_GATE_ENFORCE=true` after a clean soak + permanent regression suite + 3-agent audit + `/simplify` + close. The WriteGate CAS is still in **shadow mode** (logs would-refuse, allows) until §F.
> - **No user-facing change in §C** (an invisible reliability fix) — help files + User Manual unchanged this version; §E's recovery/collision surfaces will carry those updates.

Header buttons: **Keep** (persist via `mergeStyleOverride` + clear the live layer) · **Discard** (re-seed from the saved look + clear live → the app reverts) · close = discard. The saved look on disk is **never touched until Keep**.

> **Clean-slate rebuild after the retrofit froze 4×.** The earlier approach (unify the MIG-069 Style list onto the Presets panel) froze the main thread four times running — anything calling `unifiedStyleList`/`themeToStyle` over `BUILTIN_THEMES`; root cause never reproduced (release devtools off). Per **LL-014** it was **abandoned** and the working `StylePresetsPanel` restored (un-break `b561bafe`). The Setter is a from-scratch, **standalone** world that **touches no existing style code**: ONE preview (never a gallery of heavy cards — that was the freeze shape), a small `$state` draft (CSS-var overrides scoped to the preview via `style={draftStyle}`), Apply = direct `setProperty` on **`document.body`** (the app themes `<body>`, not `:root` — that was why Apply first did nothing). It never froze.
>
> **Two cross-subsystem fixes the editor needed to be styleable** (each Boss-validated, found by reading the code not guessing): **(1)** the note editor was a hardcoded "paper on a desk" — `NotePane.svelte` `.e-paper #fff` / `.e-desk #e8e8ec` / `.e-breadcrumb #fff`, content inheriting the **interface** font — so the Setter's Note-background + Note-font had nothing to grab. Eisa chose "make both themeable": wired to `var(--background-primary/-secondary, …)` + `font-family: var(--font-text-theme, inherit)` (each with the old value as fallback, light look preserved). The note now also follows **dark themes** (was hardcoded white = unreadable light-on-light) and matches FocusPane/CodeMirrorEditor (**Editor Parity**). **(2)** the font effect injected `.cm-editor .cm-content { font-family: <stack> !important }` (`+layout.svelte` 1694/1762/1767) — a deliberate direct CM rule (vars don't cascade into CM's scoped styles) whose `!important` beat the inherited paper font; changed to `var(--font-text-theme, <stack>) !important` — behaviour-identical (the var already holds that stack), but the content now **follows** the Setter. (Verified Eisa's `scriptFonts: {}` first to rule out the bidiPlugin per-script path.)

> **What changed in v2.48** (**MIG-067 §E/§G/§H — the Living Vocabulary becomes visible, speaks the note's language, and renders from ONE pill source**; **MIG-069 — Style Presets ship as preview cards**):
>
> **Typed links now SHOW their type, in colour, everywhere.** The 8 typed acts had stored correctly since v2.47 but rendered "all blue" — §E lands the colour: each typed link draws in its **registry colour** (the §G editor is the one source) and carries a small **type LABEL above it** in the editor. Two Settings switches gate the look — **colour typed links** · **show the label above** (both ON by default; `appSettings.colourTypedLinks` / `showTypedLinkLabels`). §G ships the **Settings → Link Types editor** (the headline feature): recolour a type and it reflects **live** everywhere — the editor links AND the Backlinks/Outgoing pills — plus a **Reset colours to default**. The registry is the single colour source; a recolour is one write every surface reads (the `livePreview` plugin subscribes to the vocabulary and dispatches a `linkVocabChanged` effect to rebuild decorations live).
>
> **Labels + pills read in the NOTE's main language, not the UI's** (§H — Eisa's rule). An Arabic note shows `يدعم` / `مشتق من`; an English note shows `supports` / `derives-from` — whatever the interface language. Detection is `dominantLocale(text)` (script→locale) → `tIn(loc, …)` (translate-in-a-specific-locale); the **editor** label reads the note body, the **panel** pills read the note title (`activeNoteName`).
>
> **One self-contained Typed-Link pill serves every surface** (§H.2 → §H.3 — the from-scratch redesign Eisa demanded: "one source serves all"). The Backlinks and Outgoing pills had been *the same component* yet still drifted — because the pill INHERITED font / text-direction / flex-alignment from each host row (two instances diverging purely from their surroundings). Rebuilt **`src/lib/components/LinkTypePill.svelte`** to be IMMUNE to its host: it sets its **own** font (`var(--font-interface-theme)`), direction (`dir="auto"`), size + shape (from `appSettings.linkPills.shape` directly, not host CSS vars), colour (the §G registry + auto-contrast text), and centring (`align-self`/`justify-content`/`vertical-align` + a 1px optical nudge). It now renders **pixel-identically** in Backlinks, Outgoing, and the **Knowledge-Health dashboard** — whose badge previously used a *hardcoded* colour map that had drifted (`supports` green there vs registry blue; now `<LinkTypePill>`, and the distribution bars fill from `linkTypeColor()`). The editor's inline label (CM6) already uses the same registry colour + note-language. **Boss-validated** ("it is clear that they all come from a single source"). **Lesson:** a *shared* component still drifts if it inherits context — make anything that must look identical everywhere fully self-contained, not merely shared.
>
> **MIG-069 — Style Presets (new migration; §C–§F Boss-validated, §G cards pending final test).** Named, **app-global** "Styles" (the VS Code Profiles model): save the current look — ticking which **sections** to include (theme · fonts · link-colours · pill-shape · typed-link-display · Sky-View · layout · behaviour) — **apply** with a click, rename / duplicate / delete, and **export / import** a shareable `<name>.constellation-style.json`, reusable across **every universe**. Storage is app-GLOBAL (`src-tauri/src/style_presets.rs` → `{app_data_dir}/style-presets.json`; frontend `src/lib/libraries/stylePresets.ts`, an 8-section catalogue). **Privacy invariant:** the *behaviour* section excludes security / tokens / folder paths (a vitest guards it). **Apply MERGES link colours** into the current universe by id — the Style wins on a conflict, the universe keeps its own custom types — and **never replaces** (the §F 3-agent audit caught a cross-universe data-loss regression where apply wiped the target's registry; fixed, plus a schema major-version gate on import). §G shows Styles as **preview CARDS** (Eisa, "like Obsidian"): each card is a **generated self-portrait** — theme paper + an `Aa` font sample + the accent pill + the 8 link-type colour dots — so a Style's *look* is visible at a glance, not a bare filename. Architect/Plan: `docs/MIG-069-style-presets-ARCHITECT-PLAN.md`; tests `tests/mig-069/` (5/5).

> ### The two decisive technical inflection points
>
> **§K — the stratum column-type latent bug.** Boss-test Stage 2 failed three consecutive times with the same "987 nodes" result. The §J.3 `diag_log_line` tracing finally revealed `cache_boot_snapshot_sky` was crashing on `Invalid column type Text at index: 4, name: stratum` — a pre-existing bug, where the column was declared TEXT in the schema but the Rust struct read it as `Option<i64>`. SQLite's loose typing meant some rows stored stratum as INTEGER, some as TEXT; the read crashed on TEXT-class rows. CNS / Sky View / Backlinks have been silently falling back to `buildSkyData` (the legacy non-federated path) all along — for who knows how long. Fix: `row.get_ref(4)` + `match` on `rusqlite::types::ValueRef::{Null, Integer, Text, Real, Blob}` to handle both storage classes.
>
> **§L — the per-schema isolation principle.** Eisa stopped the cascade with a structural insight: *"The Federation should be simple. The app shouldn't reinvent the wheel; the wheel is already there!"* — articulating the principle that each universe's data must stay its own (no merge, no integration; detachment leaves each universe intact). The Architect had locked Q3 = Option B (federated link resolution across the merged set). After §L, Q3 = Option A: each cUniverse's links resolve only within itself. The merge logic in `cache_boot_snapshot_sky` is now a per-schema loop that builds per-schema `path_to_idx` / `name_to_idx` / `alias_to_path` maps — strict isolation. Standalone-A behaves identically to A-as-cUniverse-of-B.

> ### Federation audit — 14 broken surfaces across 4 patterns
>
> Findings doc: **`docs/MIG-061-federation-audit-findings.md`**. Four parallel exploration agents surveyed every core surface. Status:
>
> | Bucket | Count | Surfaces |
> |---|---|---|
> | ✓ Federated (works) | 4 | libraryStats, Search Hub/QuickSwitcher, Lens execution, Federation Warnings popup |
> | N/A by design | 5 | 360.3D, Bookmarks, Global Tasks, Expression Forge / Sense-Making Canvas / Dashboard |
> | ◑ Partial | 1 | Org Chart (`constellation_map_universe`) — tree includes cUniverses but `load_alias_map` is parent-only |

>
> The 14 broken surfaces collapse to **four root-cause patterns**:
>
> 1. **P1 — `cache_boot_snapshot_sky` not federated** (`cache.rs:382`). One Tauri command, four dependent surfaces (CNS, Sky View, Backlinks, Outgoing). **Highest leverage / lowest risk fix.**
> 2. **P2 — Backend command uses bare `state.db` instead of `state.federated_conn`.** Six surfaces (Cataloger backend, Classifier scan + single-note, NSC, Index entries + mentions, Knowledge Health, right-sidebar previews).
> 3. **P3 — Hardcoded `{active_universe}` filesystem paths.** Three surfaces (Tag Browser, Five Acts sidebar, Workspace Bases). Each needs a per-cUniverse enumeration loop.
> 4. **P4 — FK constraints to parent's `note_meta`.** Compounds P2 for write paths (Cataloger/Classifier INSERT path). Needs schema-design decision: replicate note_meta entries / drop FK / move suggestions to per-cUniverse tables.
